text:
Vampire folklore in the U.S. is strongest in New England, especially Exeter, Rhode Island, and rural Vermont, where 19th-century communities exhumed suspected “vampires” such as Mercy Brown. Vampire tourism centers on New Orleans’ French Quarter and Forks, Washington. The only real blood-feeding bats in the country are rare common vampire bats along the far southern edge of Texas.
